```plato

    //==
    // # The isotropic element kernel
    //
    // One entry of an element stiffness matrix, for any element whose shape
    // functions have CONSTANT gradients — which is what makes the linear
    // tetrahedron and the linear triangle share this code exactly.
    //
    // Nothing here builds a strain-displacement matrix and multiplies three dense
    // matrices together. For an isotropic material the whole of B-transpose D B
    // collapses, because D holds only the two Lame constants:
    //
    //     K(i r, j s) = measure * (lambda * gi_r * gj_s
    //                              + mu * (gi_s * gj_r + (r == s ? gi . gj : 0)))
    //
    // where gi is node i's shape-function gradient and r, s are displacement
    // components. It comes straight from the elastic energy: the first term is
    // the volumetric coupling `lambda tr(eu) tr(ev)` and the second is
    // `2 mu eu : ev` with the symmetrised gradients expanded.

    // The (node i component r, node j component s) entry of an element stiffness
    // matrix. `measure` is the element's volume for a solid, or its area times a
    // thickness for a plane element.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_elasticity)
    ElasticStiffnessTerm(gi: Vector3D, gj: Vector3D, r: Integer, s: Integer,
        moduli: LameParameters, measure: Number): Number
        => measure * (moduli.FirstParameter.Pascals * gi.At(r) * gj.At(s)
            + moduli.ShearModulus.Pascals
                * (gi.At(s) * gj.At(r) + (r == s ? gi.Dot(gj) : 0.0)));
```
